title: Schooling George and Wellman Braud; bass players helping each other
summary: Garland says he taught George and gave him his first job, and schooled Braud; New Orleans bassists were friendly.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: That's the way George used to do. George used to learn things from me, cause I used to school him, you know. He used to come to my house all the time. I give him the first job he ever had.
That's what he said. That's what he said.
Yeah, he said it. That's what he said. Sure. He said that. So you would -- you would show him some changes --
Were all the New Orleans bass players friendly to each other and helpful, you seem that --
They wasn't, you know, snotty with one another.
-- play on the stand and (unintelligible) you understand?
Most bass players I know of are very nice.
You have a picture of Brow of there, Wellman Brow --
Brow's the same way, you know, I used to school Brow --
Used to have Brow come up -- with Brow come up and play, I'd get down, used to play at the Willow Lawn --
He'd come up there and play, I'd get out hide from him, wouldn't let him see me. Stand there and play, you know. Where's he -- where's old Tootie at? Where's Tootie?
Brow'd he be up there scuffling, you know. Come on out all right.
That's nice to hear, one musician talking about liking other musicians. Bass players just do.
